name: cadical
desc: Clean and efficient state-of-the-art SAT solver
why: A state-of-the-art SAT solver; genuinely fascinating to run on puzzles, though it is a serious research tool with a steep entry.

brief.what_it_is: CaDiCaL is a SAT solver, a program that decides whether a Boolean formula can be satisfied, written as a CDCL (conflict-driven clause learning) solver. Per its README, the usage is cadical [ dimacs [ proof ] ]: it takes a formula in DIMACS format as its main input and can optionally write a proof file. The homepage describes it as a clean, efficient, state-of-the-art CDCL solver. It is also available as a C library (libcadical.a) with an API.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the goal was to build a CDCL solver that is easy to understand and change while not being much slower than other state-of-the-art CDCL solvers. The author notes that the design was only partly simplified compared with Lingeling, but the code is much better documented.

commands_seen.context: Builds cadical and the library libcadical.a into the default build sub-directory. BUILD.md covers options.
Usage line from the README: runs the solver on a DIMACS input file, with an optional proof output argument.
Shows the other command-line options, according to the README.

brief.install_notes: The README documents building from source with ./configure && make rather than a binary install. The fetched text did not list compiler or toolchain requirements; BUILD.md, which I did not fetch, has the build options. The homepage links source archives (for example cadical-sc2020-45029f8.tar.xz) and the GitHub repository. Nothing about accounts, hardware, or first-run configuration appeared.
brief.standout: It is built to be read and modified, and the authors position it as a teaching-friendly alternative to heavier state-of-the-art solvers without giving up much speed. It has a strong competition record: first place in the SAT track of SAT Race 2019 and second overall.
brief.status: Unknown from the pages I read. The GitHub README shows active development, cites a CAV'24 tool paper, and mentions a NEWS.md file. However, the homepage's 'Latest Release' is the SAT Competition 2020 source archive, and I saw no release date or last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The README says CaDiCaL is missing some preprocessors, mainly parity and cardinality constraint reasoning, which it says are crucial for certain instances. Building requires ./configure && make from source. It is a serious research-grade tool, and the README is written for SAT researchers. The License badge shows MIT. The scout note calls it fun for puzzles, but the pages I read do not say that.
quotes: The goal of CaDiCaL is to provide a clean and efficient state-of-the-art CDCL solver, which is also easy to understand and change.
The goal of the development of CaDiCaL was to obtain a CDCL solver, which is easy to understand and change, while at the same time not being much slower than other state-of-the-art CDCL solvers.
